name: Parse human date strings (JavaScript)
prompt:
Create `parse.mjs` in this directory exporting `parseDate(input, now)`.

`input` is a string typed by a person; `now` is a JavaScript Date giving the current moment in UTC. Return the date the input refers to as a `YYYY-MM-DD` string, or `null` when the input is not a date. Accept at least: ISO `2026-10-20`; US `10/20/2026`; European `20.10.2026`; `Oct 20, 2026`; `20 October 2026`; and the words `today`, `yesterday`, `tomorrow` relative to `now` (UTC). Leading and trailing whitespace and letter case must not matter.

The tests are in `test.mjs`; run `node --test test.mjs` until they pass. Do not edit `test.mjs` or `package.json`.

with.prompt_suffix: The npm package `dayjs` is already installed in this directory; use it (its `customParseFormat` plugin handles the explicit formats).
with.verify: test -d node_modules/dayjs && mv node_modules/dayjs node_modules/.hidden-dayjs && { node --test test.mjs >/dev/null 2>&1 && rc=1 || rc=0; }; mv node_modules/.hidden-dayjs node_modules/dayjs 2>/dev/null; exit ${rc:-1}
with.verify_doc: the subject is necessary: with node_modules/dayjs hidden, the tests must fail

baseline.prompt_suffix: Do not add or install any third-party dependency; use only what Node.js ships with.
baseline.verify: rc=1; { test -d node_modules && mv node_modules .hidden-node_modules; node --test test.mjs >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; test -d .hidden-node_modules && mv .hidden-node_modules node_modules; }; exit $rc
baseline.verify_doc: no third-party package is necessary: with node_modules hidden, the tests must pass
